'''Shaun Livingston''' (born September 11, 1985) is an American professional [[basketball]] executive and former player. He entered the league [[NBA high school draftees|directly out of high school]] and was selected fourth by the [[Los Angeles Clippers]] in the [[2004 NBA draft]]. During his 15-year career, Livingston played 959 games for nine teams and won three [[List of NBA champions|NBA championships]] as a member of the [[Golden State Warriors#2014–2019: The dynasty|Golden State Warriors]]—in [[2015 NBA Finals|2015]], [[2017 NBA Finals|2017]], and [[2018 NBA Finals|2018]].

In February 2007, Livingston suffered a debilitating knee injury that damaged almost every part of his left knee. It took Livingston about a year and a half to return. Between 2008 and 2010, he played only 22 league games. Livingston also played for the [[Miami Heat]], [[Oklahoma City Thunder]], [[Washington Wizards]], [[Charlotte Bobcats]], [[Milwaukee Bucks]], [[Cleveland Cavaliers]], and the [[Brooklyn Nets]]. He played his last five seasons in the league with the Warriors and retired from professional basketball in September 2019.

==Early years==
Livingston was born in [[Peoria, Illinois|Peoria]], [[Illinois]]. He led Concordia Lutheran Grade School to LSA state titles in 1999 and 2000. Livingston played competitive basketball in high school at [[Richwoods High School]] for two years<ref>{{usurped|1=[https://web.archive.org/web/20080211092446/http://www.shaunlivingston14.com/about/ Shaun Livingston official website: About Shaun Livingston]}}</ref> and then transferred to [[Peoria Central High School]], where he led his team to back-to-back Class AA state titles in 2003 and 2004.

In 2004, Livingston was named [[Illinois Mr. Basketball]] and played in the [[McDonald's All-American Game]]. In 2007, he was voted one of the [[100 Legends of the IHSA Boys Basketball Tournament]] for his superior performance in the tournament.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.ihsa.org/initiatives/legends/index.htm |title=Legends of Boys Basketball |publisher=IHSA |access-date=August 30, 2012}}</ref> Considered a five-star recruit by [[Rivals.com]], Livingston was listed as the No. 1 point guard and the No. 2 player in the nation in 2004.<ref>[https://sports.yahoo.com/footballrecruiting/basketball/recruiting/player-Shaun-Livingston-8725;_ylt=Anl.TircPb0U.bBMHFIOktpGPZB4 Shaun Livingston Recruiting Profile]</ref> He committed to play college hoops at [[Duke Blue Devils men's basketball|Duke]], but opted instead to make the jump to the NBA straight out of high school.

==Professional career==

===Los Angeles Clippers (2004–2008)===
Livingston committed to [[Duke Blue Devils men's basketball|Duke]], but opted to skip college and enter the [[2004 NBA draft]], where he was selected fourth by the Los Angeles Clippers.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.dukechronicle.com/article/2004/05/deng-livingston-forgo-duke-nba-draft |title=Deng, Livingston forgo Duke for NBA Draft |last=Poses |first=Jake |publisher=Dukechronicle.com |date=May 7, 2004 |access-date=April 25, 2018}}</ref> Livingston was {{height|ft=6|in=8}}<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.palmbeachpost.com/sports/content/sports/epaper/2008/09/25/0925heat.html |title=Heat's Pat Riley: No plans to purse any veteran free agents |last=Perkins |first=Chris |date=September 25, 2008 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20080928092619/https://www.palmbeachpost.com/sports/content/sports/epaper/2008/09/25/0925heat.html |archive-date=September 28, 2008 |url-status=dead}}</ref> and was considered to be tall by point guard standards and due to the addition of [[Sam Cassell]] to the Clippers' roster, gained playing time as a [[shooting guard]] instead. Livingston recorded a career-high 14 assists on February 23, 2007, against the [[Golden State Warriors]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/games/20070224/GSWLAC/recap.html |title=Brand Throws a Block Party in Clippers' Win |work=NBA.com |date=February 24, 2007 |access-date=August 30, 2012}}</ref>

In his first two NBA seasons, Livingston played 91 games and averaged 6.3 points per game. In his third season, Livingston averaged a career-high 9.3 points per game, being one of the few Clippers to improve from the 2005–06 season.

Livingston experienced many injuries during the first three years of his professional career, missing 101 of 246 regular season games.<ref>{{cite web | title = Shaun Livingston Career Stats Page | url = http://www.nba.com/playerfile/shaun_livingston/career_stats.html | work = [[NBA.com]] | access-date = July 11, 2007 | url-status=dead | archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20070616015506/http://www.nba.com/playerfile/shaun_livingston/career_stats.html | archive-date = June 16, 2007 }}</ref><ref>{{cite web| title = Shaun Livingston Statistics | url = https://www.basketball-reference.com/players/l/livinsh01.html | publisher = Basketball-Reference.com | access-date = July 11, 2007}}</ref>

==== Knee injury ====
In a game against the [[Charlotte Bobcats]] on February 26, 2007, Livingston suffered a debilitating knee injury, dislocating his left kneecap after landing awkwardly following a missed [[layup]], resulting in the left leg snapping laterally. Livingston injured almost every part of his knee, tearing the [[anterior cruciate ligament]] (ACL), the [[posterior cruciate ligament]] (PCL), and the [[lateral meniscus]], badly spraining his [[medial collateral ligament]] (MCL), and dislocating his [[patella]] and his tibio-fibular joint.<ref name="knee2">{{cite news | url = https://www.espn.com/nba/news/story?id=2782056 | title = Livingston out for season with major knee injury | date = February 27, 2007 | access-date = July 11, 2007 | agency = Associated Press}}</ref> Livingston was told by a medical professional at the hospital that there was a chance that his leg would have to be amputated. Livingston required months of rehabilitation to be able to walk again.<ref>[http://www.grantland.com/story/_/id/8934761/on-career-shaun-livingston-survived-one-worst-injuries-nba-history Like Magic «<!-- Bot generated title -->]</ref>

===Miami Heat (2008–2009)===
Livingston's contract with the Clippers expired after the [[2007–08 NBA season|2007–08 season]], and the Clippers did not make him a $5.8 million qualifying offer, making him an unrestricted free agent.<ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.espn.com/nba/news/story?id=3481262 |title=Clippers renounce rights to Livingston, four other players |agency=Associated Press |date=July 10, 2008}}</ref> On June 16, 2008, doctors allowed Livingston to resume basketball activities;<ref name="resumes">{{cite news | url = http://articles.latimes.com/2008/jun/16/sports/spw-clippers16 | title = Shaun Livingston resumes basketball related activities | date = June 16, 2008 | access-date = June 16, 2008 | work = [[Los Angeles Times]] | url-status = dead |archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20080718005920/http://articles.latimes.com/2008/jun/16/sports/spw-clippers16 <!-- Bot retrieved archive --> |archive-date = July 18, 2008}}</ref> during the 2008 offseason, he tried to find a guaranteed contract to finalize his comeback. The [[Minnesota Timberwolves]] and [[Portland Trail Blazers]] were interested, but it was reported Livingston eventually signed a two-year deal with the [[Miami Heat]] on October 3, 2008. In four games with the Heat, he averaged 2.3 points and 10.3 minutes.<ref name="espngrizzlies" /><ref>{{cite news |url=http://www.nba.com/heat/news/heat_sign_shaun_livingston.html |title=HEAT Sign Shaun Livingston |work=NBA.com |date=October 4, 2008}}</ref>

=== Tulsa 66ers (2009) ===
On January 7, 2009, Livingston was traded to the [[Memphis Grizzlies]] along with cash considerations for a conditional 2012 second-round pick.<ref name="espngrizzlies" /><ref>{{cite web | url=http://www.nba.com/grizzlies/news/grizzlies_trade_second_round_pick_to_miami-090107.html |title=Grizzlies trade conditional second round draft pick to Miami | work=[[NBA.com]] |date=January 7, 2009 | access-date =January 7, 2009}}</ref> He was then waived later that same day.<ref name="espngrizzlies">{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/news/story?id=3817147 |title=Heat trade Livingston to Grizzlies |publisher=[[ESPN]] |date=January 7, 2009 |access-date=August 30, 2012}}</ref><ref>{{cite web | url=http://www.nba.com/grizzlies/news/grizzlies_waive_shaun_livingston-090107.html |title=Grizzlies waive Shaun Livingston | work=[[NBA.com]] |date=January 7, 2009 | access-date =January 7, 2009}}</ref> On March 7, 2009, Livingston signed with the [[Tulsa 66ers]], the [[NBA Development League|NBA development league]] team owned by the [[Oklahoma City Thunder]].<ref name="espngrizzlies" /><ref>{{cite news |first=Kevin|last=Henry|url=http://newsok.com/ex-clipper-livingston-joins-66ers/article/3351554?custom_click=headlines_widget |title= Ex-Clipper Livingston joins 66ers  |publisher=NewsOK.com |date=March 8, 2009|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160307125947/http://newsok.com/ex-clipper-livingston-joins-66ers/article/3351554?custom_click=headlines_widget|archive-date=March 7, 2016}}</ref>

=== Oklahoma City Thunder (2009) ===
After three weeks with the 66ers, Livingston signed a multi-year deal with the Thunder on March 31, 2009.<ref>[https://web.archive.org/web/20090504012948/http://basketball.realgm.com/src_wiretap_archives/58212/20090331/oklahoma_city_signs_shaun_livingston Shaun Livingston Signs Multi-Year Deal] March 31, 2009</ref> On December 22, he was waived by the Thunder.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.nba.com/thunder/news/thunder_aquires_maynor_2009_12_22.html |title=Thunder Acquires Maynor From Utah Jazz |work=NBA.com |date=December 22, 2009 | access-date=July 14, 2010}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.dailythunder.com/2009/12/thunder-acquires-eric-maynor-from-jazz-waives-livingston-and-wilks |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110708222004/http://www.dailythunder.com/2009/12/thunder-acquires-eric-maynor-from-jazz-waives-livingston-and-wilks/ |url-status=dead |archive-date=July 8, 2011 |title=Thunder acquires Eric Maynor from Jazz, waives Livingston and Wilks |publisher=Daily Thunder.com |date=December 22, 2009 |access-date=August 30, 2012 }}</ref>

=== Washington Wizards (2010) ===
On February 26, 2010, Livingston signed the first of his two 10-day contracts with the [[Washington Wizards]].<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.nba.com/wizards/news/livingston_100226.html |title=Wizards Sign Guard Shaun Livingston |work=NBA.com |date=February 26, 2010 | access-date=July 14, 2010}}</ref> Eventually, Livingston was then signed for the rest of the season.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.nba.com/wizards/news/livingston_100319.html |title=Wizards Sign Livingston For Remainder of the Season |work=NBA.com |date=March 19, 2010 | access-date=July 14, 2010}}</ref>

=== Charlotte Bobcats (2010–2011) ===
On July 20, 2010, Livingston signed a two-year contract worth $7 million with the [[Charlotte Bobcats]].<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.nba.com/bobcats/release_livingston_signed_100720.html |title=Bobcats Sign Point Guard Shaun Livingston |work=NBA.com |date=July 20, 2010 |access-date=July 20, 2010 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20100723103955/http://www.nba.com/bobcats/release_livingston_signed_100720.html |archive-date=July 23, 2010 }}</ref>

=== Milwaukee Bucks (2011–2012) ===
On June 23, 2011, Livingston was traded to the [[Milwaukee Bucks]] as part of a three-way deal that included the [[Sacramento Kings]] and [[Charlotte Bobcats]].<ref>{{cite web | title=Bucks acquire Jackson, Livingston, Udrih and draft rights to Tobias Harris in a three-team trade | work=NBA.com | url=http://www.nba.com/bucks/release/draft_trade_110623.html | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110627231238/http://www.nba.com/bucks/release/draft_trade_110623.html | archive-date=June 27, 2011 | date=June 23, 2011| access-date=June 29, 2011}}</ref>

=== Return to Washington (2012) ===
[[File:Shaun Livingston Washington at Orlando 054 (cropped).jpg|thumb|right|Livingston in 2012]]
On June 26, 2012, Livingston was traded to the [[Houston Rockets]] for [[Samuel Dalembert]] along with teammates [[Jon Leuer]] and [[Jon Brockman]].<ref>{{cite web |title=Rockets Receive 12th Overall Pick Via Trade With Bucks |work=[[NBA.com]] |url=http://www.nba.com/rockets/news/rockets-receive-12th-overall-pick-trade-bucks |date=June 27, 2012 |access-date=June 27, 2012}}</ref> However, they were all waived before the beginning of the season.<ref>{{cite web |title=Rockets trim roster to 15, waive Livingston |work=[[SB Nation|The Dream Shake]] |url=http://www.thedreamshake.com/2012/10/29/3573082/rockets-trim-roster-to-15-waive-livingston |date=October 29, 2012 |access-date=October 29, 2012}}</ref> On November 15, Livingston re-signed with the [[Washington Wizards]].<ref>[http://www.nba.com/wizards/news/wizards-sign-shaun-livingston Wizards Sign Shaun Livingston]</ref> He was waived on December 23.<ref>[http://www.nba.com/wizards/news/wizards-waive-livingston-and-barron Wizards Waive Livingston And Barron]</ref>

=== Cleveland Cavaliers (2012–2013) ===
On December 25, 2012, the [[Cleveland Cavaliers]] claimed Livingston off waivers after releasing [[Donald Sloan (basketball)|Donald Sloan]].<ref>[http://www.nba.com/cavaliers/releases/livingston-sloan-121225 Cavaliers Claim Shaun Livingston Off Waivers, Waive Donald Sloan]</ref><ref>[http://www.nba.com/2012/news/12/25/cavaliers-shaun-livingstone-claimed.ap/index.html?ls=iref:nbahpts Cavaliers claim Livingston]</ref> Livingston made his debut for the Cavaliers on January 2, 2013, recording two points, two rebounds, and one assist in 13 minutes of action off the bench.

===Brooklyn Nets (2013–2014)===
On July 11, 2013, Livingston signed with the [[Brooklyn Nets]].<ref>[http://www.insidehoops.com/blog/?p=13718 Brooklyn Nets sign guard Shaun Livingston]</ref> His season-high of 23 points came in a 108–98 loss to the Portland Trail Blazers on November 18.<ref>[https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=400489023 Trail Blazers surge past Nets for 7th straight win]</ref> Initially billed as a backup, Livingston performed well enough to join [[Deron Williams]] in the starting lineup following a season-ending injury to [[Brook Lopez]]. With Livingston on the floor, the Nets proved to be 8.5 points per 100 possessions better defensively, and he earned the third-most minutes on the team.<ref>[http://hangtime.blogs.nba.com/2014/03/12/livingston-embodies-nets-new-identity/ LIVINGSTON EMBODIES NETS’ NEW IDENTITY]</ref> On March 17, 2014, Livingston set a career-high for both minutes played and points scored in a season.<ref>[https://www.washingtonpost.com/blogs/wizards-insider/wp/2014/03/21/shaun-livingston-resurrects-his-career-with-brooklyn-nets/ Shaun Livingston resurrects his career with Brooklyn Nets]</ref> At the end of the season, he had played in a career-high 76 games (beating a previous high of 61 games) and averaged 8.3 points, 3.2 assists, and 1.2 steals per game.

===Golden State Warriors (2014–2019)===
On July 11, 2014, Livingston signed with the [[Golden State Warriors]]<ref>[http://www.nba.com/warriors/news/warriors-sign-livingston-20140711 Warriors Sign Free Agent Shaun Livingston to Contract]</ref> for a reported three-year, $16 million contract.<ref>[http://basketball.realgm.com/wiretap/234077/Warriors-Reach-Three-Year-$16M-Deal-With-Shaun-Livingston Warriors Reach Three-Year, $16M Deal With Shaun Livingston]</ref> On August 15, he was ruled out for six to eight weeks after having arthroscopic surgery on the big toe of his right foot.<ref>[http://www.nba.com/2014/news/08/15/livingston-surgery.ap/ Warriors' Livingston out 6-8 weeks with toe injury]</ref> Livingston recovered in time to make his Warriors debut in the season opener and served as a key player off the bench for the Warriors in their run to the [[2015 NBA Finals|2015 NBA Championship]] while becoming an integral member of the Warriors dynasty.<ref>[https://www.basketball-reference.com/players/l/livinsh01/gamelog/2015/ Shaun Livingston 2014-15 Game Log]</ref>

In [[2015–16 NBA season|2015–16]], Livingston helped the Warriors win an NBA record 73 games to eclipse the 72 wins set by the [[1995–96 Chicago Bulls season|1995–96 Chicago Bulls]]. During Game 4 of the 2016 Western Conference semi-finals, Livingston was ejected late in the second quarter against the Portland Trail Blazers. He had moved into the starting lineup to accommodate for the injured [[Stephen Curry]]. In the Western Conference Finals, the Warriors overcame a 3–1 deficit to defeat the [[Oklahoma City Thunder]] in seven games and advance to the [[2016 NBA Finals]]. In Game 1 of the NBA Finals against the [[Cleveland Cavaliers]], Livingston scored a playoff career-high 20 points, leading the Warriors to a 104–89 victory.<ref>[http://www.nba.com/games/20160602/CLEGSW/gameinfo.html Warriors' supporting cast leads Game 1 NBA Finals win]</ref> Despite the Warriors going up 3–1 in the series following a Game 4 victory, they went on to lose the series in seven games.

In [[2016–17 NBA season|2016–17]], Livingston helped the Warriors win the NBA Championship after defeating the Cavaliers 4–1 in the [[2017 NBA Finals]]. The Warriors finished the playoffs with a 16–1 record, the best postseason winning percentage in NBA history.<ref>{{cite web |date=June 14, 2017 |title=Warriors (16–1) Record Best Postseason Winning Percentage in NBA History |url=https://bleacherreport.com/articles/2715556-warriors-16-1-record-best-postseason-winning-percentage-in-nba-history |access-date=May 10, 2018 |website=Bleacher Report}}</ref>

On July 25, 2017, Livingston re-signed with the Warriors<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/warriors/news/six-players-re-signing-20170725|title=Warriors Re-Sign Curry, Durant, Iguodala, Livingston, Pachulia and West to Contracts|work=NBA.com|date=July 25, 2017|access-date=July 25, 2017}}</ref> on a three-year, $24 million contract.<ref>{{cite web|last=Haynes|first=Chris|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/story/_/id/19779630/golden-state-warriors-re-sign-shaun-livingston|title=Shaun Livingston staying with Warriors on 3-year, $24 million deal|work=ESPN.com|date=July 1, 2017|access-date=July 21, 2017}}</ref> On December 4, he was suspended for one game without pay for an altercation with game official Courtney Kirkland during a game against the [[Miami Heat]] a day earlier.<ref>{{Cite web |title=NBA official Courtney Kirkland and Warriors' Shaun Livingston suspended |url=https://pr.nba.com/courtney-kirkland-shaun-livingston-suspensions/ |access-date=November 22, 2022 |website=NBA|date=December 4, 2017 }}</ref> Livingston helped the Warriors win back-to-back titles in [[2018 NBA Finals|2018]] after defeating the Cavaliers in a four-game sweep in the Finals.

In 2019, Livingston played in his fifth straight [[2019 NBA Finals|NBA Finals]], where the Warriors lost to the [[Toronto Raptors]] in six games. Livingston's final NBA game was in Game 6 of the final series (played on June 13, 2019, with the Warriors losing 114–110), where he recorded six points and a steal in 16 minutes of playing time.

On July 10, 2019, Livingston was waived by the Warriors.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.nba.com/warriors/news/livingston-waived-20190710|title=Warriors Waive Guard Shaun Livingston|work=NBA.com|date=July 10, 2019}}</ref>

On September 13, 2019, Livingston announced his retirement from the NBA. In a post, Livingston stated: "After 15 years in the NBA, I’m excited, sad, fortunate and grateful all in one breath. Hard to put into a caption all of the emotions it takes to try and accomplish your dreams."<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.nba.com/article/2019/09/13/shaun-livingston-announces-retirement |title=Shaun Livingston announces retirement from NBA |website=NBA.com |language=en |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20201129222520/http://www.nba.com/news/shaun-livingston-announces-retirement |archive-date=2020-11-29 |url-status=live |access-date=2019-12-06 }}</ref>

==Post-playing career==
On September 15, 2020, the [[Golden State Warriors]] announced that they had named Livingston as director of players affairs and engagement.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.nba.com/warriors/news/livingston-new-role-20200915|title=Warriors Name Shaun Livingston Director of Player Affairs and Engagement 14-Year NBA Veteran Won Three Championships with Golden State|date=September 15, 2020|website=NBA.com|access-date=September 15, 2020}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.nytimes.com/athletic/2046440/2020/09/14/thompson-shaun-livingstons-purposeful-decision-to-sign-on-as-a-warriors-exec/|title=Thompson: Shaun Livingston's purposeful decision to sign on as a Warriors exec|website=theathletic.com|language=en|access-date=2020-09-15}}</ref> He won his fourth [[List of NBA champions|NBA championship]] after the Warriors defeated the [[Boston Celtics]] in six games in the [[2022 NBA Finals]]. Livingston left the role on June 20, 2023, citing a desire to spend more time with his family outside of the Bay Area.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Delucchi |first=Marc |date=2023-06-20 |title=Shaun Livingston decides to leave Warriors front office after three years |url=https://www.goldenstateofmind.com/2023/6/20/23767447/shaun-livingston-leaves-golden-state-warriors-front-office |access-date=2023-12-04 |website=Golden State Of Mind |language=en}}</ref>

==Personal life==
Livingston is a [[Lutheranism|Lutheran]]. In April 2016, he donated $1 million to his former grade school, Concordia Lutheran School, in Peoria, Illinois.<ref>{{cite news | last=Adams | first=Pam | title=NBA Player Shaun Livingston jump-starts Concordia Lutheran School renovations with $1 million donation | url=http://www.pjstar.com/news/20160426/nba-player-shaun-livingston-jump-starts-concordia-lutheran-school-renovations-with-1-million-donation | website=PJStar.com | date=April 26, 2016 | archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20160630173624/http://www.pjstar.com/news/20160426/nba-player-shaun-livingston-jump-starts-concordia-lutheran-school-renovations-with-1-million-donation | archive-date = 2016-06-30 | url-status = dead | access-date=2024-02-06}}  Also {{cite news | last=Adams | first=Pam | title = Livingston kick-starts Concordia renovations - NBA player and alumnus boosts project with $1 million donation | page = 3A | date=April 27, 2016 | work = [[Peoria Journal Star]] | location = Peoria, Illinois | edition = text | via = [[NewsBank]] | url = https://infoweb.newsbank.com/apps/news/openurl?ctx_ver=z39.88-2004&rft_id=info%3Asid/infoweb.newsbank.com&svc_dat=NewsBank&req_dat=820AFA7A248C4E9FA06AC9A554EEF8BD&rft_val_format=info%3Aofi/fmt%3Akev%3Amtx%3Actx&rft_dat=document_id%3Anews%252F15CA17540C0656B0 | url-access = subscription }}</ref>
